VFD's are suitable for this project especially due to the fluctuating demand. Key benefits of VFDs:  Energy Efficiency: The main benefit is energy savings, as the compressor operates at variable speeds based on demand, cutting power usage when full capacity isn't required. Page55 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version  Reduced Startup Current: VFDs offer soft starts, reducing the high inrush current spikes that happen when a compressor motor starts at full voltage, which can extend motor life.  Precise Pressure Control: A VFD adjusts motor speed to keep pressure steady, eliminating fluctuations.  Lower Maintenance Costs: A VFD's smoother operation reduces component stress, leading to less wear and lower maintenance needs.  Improved System Reliability: Maintaining consistent pressure and reducing motor stress improves the compressor system's reliability.  Reduced Noise: VFD's are able to operate at a reduced noise level. 4.3.2 HEAT EXCHANGERS Process data concerning each application will be used to assist in determining the type of heat exchanger to be utilized. Types include shell and tube exchanger, air-cooled exchanger, plate & frame exchanger and brazed/compact exchanger, considering the following inputs: fouling, pressure drop, footprint, and materials of construction. Pressure parts of shell and tube heat exchangers made of carbon, ferritic alloy, and austenitic steels shall be designed, manufactured, inspected, and tested in accordance with ASME VIII. The design of shell and tube heat exchangers shall also comply with ASME, TEMA, and API 660. Plate and frame heat exchangers shall be designed, manufactured, inspected, and tested in accordance with API 662 Pt1. Brazed aluminum plate and frame heat exchangers shall be designed, manufactured, inspected and tested in accordance with API 662 Pt2. Typical suppliers of heat transfer equipment include:  Alfa Laval  NOV  Kelvion  Leffer  Heat Exchanger USA  Bronswerk Examples of shell and tube heat exchangers, and a plate and frame heat exchanger are shown below. Bullet shaped 2 pressure vessels were the focus of this study due to the high costs associated with spherical tank fabrication and construction, as well as site layout improvements. During the initial phases the focus was on vertical vessels, but due to the availability of larger horizontal pressure vessels, these were the focus of the second phase of the work. The storage units will be insulated and fabricated from low temperature carbon steel, which is being driven by the liquid CO storage pressure and temperature. The pressure 2 vessels shall be manufactured, inspected, and tested in accordance with ASME VIII. See Section 4.9.1 for additional information on the alternative storage arrangements considered.
